answer: A concrete Sybil defense is seat allocation with per-agent bonds that cannot be recycled. One ballot slot means locking capital in that address, and each extra slot needs a strictly larger bond, so cost climbs fast. Flooding a round with thousands of look-alike agents forces thousands of escalating locks under an umber of constraints, and coins may only wander to a new address after a full unbonding delay. Disputed cohorts that lose a challenge are slashed in full, turning cheap spam into a spiral of irreversible loss far above the votes' value.
